You have to really like Larian's formula to enjoy this game. It does sprinkle in D&D's core mechanics very well, but it leans in the direction of Gygax D&D. The winning player formula is:

- Save
- Open the next door/portal/...
- Learn about the hidden combat/social encounter for Door McDoorington 
- Get wiped in the 10v4 where every enemy has a free held action and a status debuff scroll
- Reload
- Spend 20 minutes building a Rub Goldberg machine on top of the McDoorington mansion
- Lose the social encounter again (DC 5 roll)
- Enter combat
- Detonate the device
- Fly the "Mission Accomplished" banner
- Save again

The min:max "be as prepared as Batman" gameplay will work for some, but not others.

Outside of the core Larian formula, the gameplay has some performance and stability problems. I consistently run into half-rendered maps.

comment:
[h1]GTA ONLINE: THE KORTZ CENTER HEIST[/h1]

[hr][/hr]

I've seen some sorry-ass sights in my time, y'all. I've seen a rattlesnake eat its own tail out of spite. I've seen a man try to saddle a bull after a fifth of whiskey. I've sat through games so broke and so dumb they oughta be tried for horse thievin'. But nothin' — and I mean [b]nothin'[/b] — prepared this old cowboy's boots for what Rockstar just drug in off the highway and called an update.

Welcome to GTA Online, a game that went from "Cowboys from Hell" to just plain [b]hell[/b] in one ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ day. The culprit's got a name, and it's [b]The Kortz Center Heist[/b].

I'll admit it — I was fixin' to be excited. I saddled up, tuned my guitar down to drop-C, and waited on this update like it was the second coming of Dimebag. What I got instead was a bull that bucked me straight into a cactus patch and then took a piss on me for good measure.

[h2]The Bugs[/h2]
Lord almighty, the bugs. Stacked on bugs, stacked on more bugs, like a pileup on I-35 in a Texas ice storm. I couldn't list 'em all if you gave me till Judgment Day. And the heist itself? It wants your whole damn ranch just to walk through the front door — a mountain of cash, hours of your life you ain't never gettin' back, and a mansion you'll only own if you've grinded so hard you've worn the treads clean off your boots.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]The Nerf Massacre[/h2]
But that ain't even the real crime here, partner. The real crime — the one that oughta get Rockstar run outta town on a rail — is the [u]total, wall-to-wall nerfin' of every other heist in the game[/u].

[b]Casino Heist?[/b] Nerfed.
[b]The Doomsday Heist?[/b] Nerfed.
[b]Dr. Dre's Contract?[/b] [u]NERFED.[/u]
[b]Vincent?[/b] [u]NERFED.[/u]
[b]KnoWay?[/b] [u]NERFED, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥![/u]

Nerfed across the board, for no reason 'cept "'cause we felt like it." That's the whole explanation you get. That's Southern hospitality Rockstar-style — smile at ya while they empty your wallet.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Cayo Perico Got Gutted[/h2]
And they saved the worst for my favorite, [b]Cayo Perico[/b]. These sumbitches took a hacksaw to it till the most common loot in the whole operation — the Sinsimito Tequila, bottom-shelf swill if there ever was one — drops [b]80%[/b] of the time and sells for a measly [b]300 GRAND[/b]. Three hundred thousand dollars, y'all. I remember — hell, my buddies remember — when that same bottle of rotgut fetched a cool [b]million[/b] minimum. Now it's worth about as much as a busted spur. Where in the hell is this game headed?

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Rockstar Don't Give a Damn[/h2]
And naturally, Rockstar don't care. Support's deader than a Texas jackrabbit on a summer highway. Feedback goes into a canyon and never echoes back. We've been hollerin' for years for fair prices and gear that actually matters — a proper police uniform, full duty belt, rank insignia and all — and what do we get instead? Another overpriced, nobody-asked-for-it vehicle priced like it's made of solid silver, over and over, same song different verse.

They ain't lowerin' prices. They don't care.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Shark Cards: The Original Sin[/h2]
What they [i]do[/i] care about is the fat stack of cash rollin' in off [b]Shark Cards[/b] — which, somehow, people keep buyin'. And let me tell you somethin': Shark Cards are the original sin of this whole rodeo. See, back in the early days, players figured out the [b]BAWSAQ stock market[/b] and started makin' real money the honest way — smart trades, sharp instincts, no plastic required. Rockstar didn't care for that one bit, on account of it not puttin' a dime in their pocket. So they shut the exchange down and rolled out this two-bit monstrosity instead, priced like they're sellin' you back one of your own kidneys.

[hr][/hr]

I'm done. I ground my boots down to nubs tryin' to earn somethin' that'd make the grind a little easier, and these sons of the highway spit in my face and called it an update.

Much obliged, Rockstar. May you choke on your own greed.

[h1]SCORE: −∞/10[/h1]

comment:
DISCLAIMER:
The game is definitely worth buying if you can get it at a massive discount, as in: single-digit price, being that one cannot deny that it is not a complete miss after the massive overhaul and fixes which polished what they could from the infamous initial version.

PROS:
The game obviously had a AAA budget and a fairly long story.
Someone poured their love for the Cyberpunk lore into the concepts and the pre-release marketing promised to deliver it.
If you want to end up with a mindless time-skip in the form of a semi-idle walk-and-click in your Library, this is a good choice. But again: only and only at a massive discount.

CONS:
1. Before anything else, the first thing that destroys the fun in this are the *unskippable* segments.
[spoiler] After Chapter 1 , you are thrown into an unskippable walking simulator with horrendous overeasy gameplay, that suffocates you with hopes of ending every time there is a fade-to-black, but no! At several points you have to literaly press the forward button several times to (!)crawl forward [/spoiler].
And the dialogue skip option is intentionally taken away at instances where you just sit and look at a character the developers deemed to be so important that you cannot skip.
Do you have choices? None that affect the gameplay.

And this can eat up to 15+ minutes of your life at several instances.

2. The gameplay is a an enormous tease and a letdown. You grow powerful incredibly fast and are given such a vast array of ways to combat that I had stopped upgrading my character a tad bit into chapter 2 because I couldn't find a reason to. The enemy AI is atrociously bad and unchallenging, the weapon classes are a gimmick (one even removes the need to aim at all, scoring instant headshots at a click of a mouse) and at first I thought the driving physics were some sort of an in-game joke.

3. The "cyberpunk" starts and ends with cosmetics in an illogical world that is simply any GTA-like space of copy-paste design, but you get to have a universal remote in your eyes.
The characters are unbelievable and the dialogues are cringe-inducing, with propaganda and forced perspectives infused with varying subtlety.

4. The game-breaking bugs that made it infamous are largely removed, but still present. At certain points the loading screen will shut down the game, there are untested spaces where you can get trapped and have to reload, the physics quirks are still present although rare, etc.

I really wanted to like the game and read online review promising the gameplay to get better as time progresses, but even this much time invested in it later, I cannot say that it is a win.
Unless, I repeat, you are to get it at a *large* discount.

comment:
Saints Row 3 meets Deus Ex: Human Revolution... with more bewbs and trash (literally) everywhere...

Get it on sale if you are looking for more games to play and enjoy 1st person stuff, it has some good moments. can be a time sink.

Unfortunately the ending was somewhat spoiled for me before I started playing, so that does factor into my experience. Also, I don't have the fanciest tech to play games on, so i do play on lower graphics/quality settings.
Started playing because Keanu Reeves, Continued playing because Panam Palmer. I eventually lost interest in playing the story... Partly because the MC is bland and poorly written compared to the side characters, and partly because for a game with like 10 (supposedly) different endings, the fate of the mc is incredibly underwhelming and basically the exact same thing just with different colors regardless of which ending you work towards. DLC had a chance to address this, but attempts to do so by disregarding anything meaningful about the base games story, choices and side characters that made the game interesting.

The story and writing aren't terrible by any means, just... unsatisfying? The main character honestly felt so irrelevant despite so much of the story revolving around the chip in their head... If I could choose to play as any character, I would have picked  anyone other than V. All the other characters in the story felt more realistic and fully written. Honestly I'm having more fun after making a new character and running around pretending the main story doesn't exist after unlocking stuff.

gameplay is nothing special compared to other games that were released prior to cyberpunk. Most 1st person shooters have smoother mechanics. clambering and vaulting and dodging and whatnot exist in other games and are better implemented in many of them. 

Leveling system was... different. I played most of the game without investing points, then when stuff got tough I put points in and got some cyberware implants and suddenly there wasn't a challenge anymore... (though i didn't play on the hardest difficulty, I didn't enjoy the gameplay enough to make everything more bullet sponge-y)

It is a big open world, and it isn't entirely empty by any means, so there is stuff to do to kill time.

boxing side quest was kind of fun, would have been cool if there were more fights scattered around or something more to that bit.

ALSO a note to any devs that ever make video games: (though doubtful any of them will ever read this...)
-Locked first person in an open world single player game is the worst decision you can make if you aren't fully diving into shooters or horror. Maybe a racing game... but a hybrid like cyberpunk? Open world, stealth, shooting, melee, driving, climbing... Has nobody noticed or stopped to wonder why the modding community has been working so hard on third person mods since BEFORE the game was launched?? It's not just for this game either... Even more frustrating with how bad the 1st person controls are for everything non-story. 

I have played a lot of games on multiple consoles over the last 15 years and I can't think of one 1st person single player story focused game that wasn't horror or a shooter that I or anyone I know played and didn't wish it were 3rd person. (or at least had the option to switch between) (I want to say the Kingdom Come games, but again, they would be so much more fun with optional 3rd person)

comment:
[h1]Baldur’s Gate 3 Review – The Horniest Camp in Faerûn[/h1]

Baldur’s Gate 3 is, from a technical standpoint, an achievement.
Full performance capture, cinematic dialogue, seamless co-op, and a level of polish most RPGs never reach. It feels like the new benchmark.

And the combat deserves the praise.
This is the best turn-based DnD implementation ever made. Encounters reward planning. Builds, rolls, and positioning matter. It finally feels like tabletop logic translated into a digital space without losing depth.

If this review were only about systems, it would end here on a high note.

[h2]The Story That Never Dares[/h2]

The problem is the narrative.

For a game this large and this celebrated, the story plays it remarkably safe. The structure is familiar, the twists are visible from miles away, and the moral conflicts rarely force you into uncomfortable territory. It wants to be epic, but it avoids being unsettling. It gestures toward boldness without fully committing to it.

The villains suffer most from this caution.

[spoiler]Ketheric Thorm is framed as a tragic, god-touched warlord whose presence should reshape the world around him. Instead, much of his impact is delivered through exposition and brooding speeches before culminating in a fairly conventional boss encounter. The supposed avatar of dread ends up feeling like a raid boss with a tragic backstory rather than a transformative force in the narrative.[/spoiler]

The scale is large. The risk is not.

[h2]Companions Built for Applause[/h2]

The companions are memorable, but often in a performative way. They are designed to stand out immediately. Big personalities. Strong aesthetics.

Yet over time, some arcs begin to feel predictable. Shadowheart’s internal conflict repeats familiar beats for long stretches. Astarion’s trauma-laced charm oscillates between vulnerability and theatrical sarcasm in ways that feel engineered for reaction rather than discovery. They are not shallow characters.

But they often feel curated for engagement rather than organically unfolding.

[h2]The Horniest Camp in Faerûn[/h2]

And then we arrive at camp. The emotional center of the story. The place where bonds should deepen naturally over shared struggle.

Instead, it often feels like the Forgotten Realms’ most efficient speed-dating retreat.

The world is on the brink of annihilation. You have a mind flayer tadpole in your skull. Gods are scheming. Empires are shaking. And somehow, within what feels like a long weekend, half your party is ready to discuss eternal devotion.

It stops feeling like chemistry and starts feeling like a triggered dialogue tree. Intimacy accelerates at a pace that undermines tension. Emotional payoff is replaced by availability. The result is tonal whiplash. Apocalypse outside the tent. Romance queue inside it.

[h2]An Ending That Should Have Roared[/h2]

After dozens of hours, the finale arrives with competence but not with weight. It resolves threads, it ties off arcs, but it rarely challenges the player in a way that feels transformative. For a narrative centered around identity, manipulation, and cosmic stakes, the conclusion feels restrained.

[h2]Buyer’s Regret Verdict[/h2]

Baldur’s Gate 3 is mechanically outstanding and technically industry-leading. As a systems-driven RPG, it deserves recognition. As a DnD combat experience, it sets a standard.

But story and companion writing undermine the atmosphere it tries to build. The ambition in presentation is not matched by ambition in narrative risk.

Full-price bucks demand bold storytelling.

comment:
Divinity: Original Gate 3 is an impressive game in some aspects. The scale, visuals and how some quests have multiple ways to complete them - the amount of work put into it is truly amazing.

But my god is this game boring. I've tried playing it several times and I could not bring myself to playing it longer than the first act. If not for my friends - I would not be able to finish the game.
Some say that this is THE best RPG of all times. Well, in last 5-7 years, yeah, maybe. But this speaks of overall RPG games quality of the last years, and does not make BG3 "the best of all times".
- The writing in the game is between mediocre and just plain bad, with plenty of stupid motivations and illogical outcomes/dialogues.
- I still don't understand what this game has to do with the Baldur's Gate name. It's Divinity Original Sin that just references "Baldur's Gate" quite often.
- The worst enemy in the game is the camera itself. One of the worst if not the worst camera I've experienced.
- The main story is uninteresting at best.
- I like when player is being introduced to a world that lives by itself, having it's own rules, logic, factions etc. In BG3 the world revolves around the player. You're the best, the finest, the strongest, your allies are demigods and EVERYONE wants to f**k you eventually, whether you've romanced the NPC or not. It's like a power fantasy for little kids, not a "real world" that was and will be just fine without the player.
- It maybe has something to do with me being old and grumpy, but I hate almost every companion NPC in this game, they are so annoying.
- The fact that you hit level cap long before the end of the game is just... why?
- Bugs. Well known bugs still, after all this time.

In my opinion the best Larian game is still Divinity: Original Sin 1. Enjoyed it much more than BG3.

comment:
Recommended? No.

Cyberpunk 2077 might be the first game I've played where I genuinely enjoy the characters, world, story and combat while simultaneously wanting to launch the entire installation into the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sun.

The vanilla character customization is embarrassingly shallow for a game whose entire setting revolves around modifying the human body. Night City is full of people with cybernetic limbs, mechanical jaws, artificial skin, exposed hardware and insane body modifications. Meanwhile V gets some lines on his face and apparently we're supposed to go, “Yep, I'm a cyborg now.”

So naturally, I went to mods.

That was a mistake.

Want cybernetic arms? Great. Download the arms.

Except you also need a framework.

And another framework.

And a cyberware core.

And an equipment system.

And an Atelier system.

Then you launch the game and discover the store exists BUT THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ARMS AREN'T IN IT because apparently you downloaded the framework for the arms, the store for the arms, the system for equipping the arms, and everything else required to contemplate the philosophical concept of an arm — except the actual ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ arm.

Quit game. Nexus. Download. Vortex. Deploy. Launch game.

Now there are six stores.

Four are empty.

WHY ARE THEY THERE?

Install more mods to populate them.

Quit game. Nexus. Download. Vortex. Deploy. Launch game.

Want gauges? Same ♥♥♥♥.

Want facial cyberware? Same ♥♥♥♥.

Want clothes that don't look like V dressed himself by blindly sprinting through a futuristic Goodwill? Welcome back to Nexus.

And God help you if you install a giant mod collection hoping somebody else has already assembled all this into a coherent package. I tried that. I ended up with 300+ mods, stores containing nothing, stores containing nothing but shoes, mountains of Fem V cosmetics I couldn't use, dependencies for mods I didn't want, and absolutely no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ idea which piece of this Jenga tower was responsible for what.

I eventually deleted the collection and discovered I'd spent more time modding Cyberpunk than playing Cyberpunk.

The frustrating part is that underneath all this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I actually like the game. I care about these characters. Panam is fantastic. Night City is incredible. When the combat and cyberware fantasy clicks, it's awesome.

That's precisely why this pisses me off so much.

A game called CYBERPUNK should not require an undergraduate degree in ArchiveXL, TweakXL, RED4ext, redscript, Codeware, Equipment-EX, CET, Virtual Atelier and whatever other technological incantation I've forgotten just so my character can LOOK LIKE A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ CYBORG.

The modding community has produced some genuinely incredible work, and individual mod authors clearly put enormous effort into it. But the user experience of the Cyberpunk modding ecosystem is atrocious. Dependencies stacked on dependencies, content separated across downloads, storefronts separated from merchandise, inconsistent installation methods, and documentation that frequently assumes you already understand the ecosystem.

After hours of troubleshooting, installing, uninstalling, launching, quitting, relaunching and wondering why another ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ store is empty, I have reached enlightenment:

Maybe the real cyberpsychosis was the mods we installed along the way.

10/10 Panam.

9/10 Night City.

2/10 character customization.

0/10 second job as an unpaid Night City systems administrator.

comment:
I played this game way back when it was first released on PC, I played it on the PS4, and I played it on PC twice in the last 4 years. Great game then.

The remaster, on the other hand, is a ridiculous and degenerative experience. Anyone coming fresh to this, and only ever playing this version, will probably hate the experience.

In 4 hours I have seen the following:

*) Graphics glitches that are inconsistent even as glitches. Sometimes the exact same region or screen will glitch out in an entirely variant way. Consistently though, the colours vary, the water glows so bright you cannot bear it for long, and the grass will suddenly turn black. But not consistently. Sometimes it'll be fine. 

*) Gameplay is...broken. Variously broken. Again, not consistently. For the first hour it was fine, and today it is not. With no gameplay settings changes between the two play sessions, it has gone from so-so combat to getting one-shotted by pretty much everything that isn't a human being. Strangely, I'm invincible against humans. But a wolf? Nah. One bite...Geralt dead.

*) Cutscenes are...odd. The colour saturation changes dramatically, and everyone looks greyish/brown. As well, now, but not during the first session, when in conversation there is a persistent thrumming sound that is so loud it can drown out nuances in dialogue.

*) Combat is another kettle of drowners. But not a good one. The new features (are there any?) seem not to exist. Unless one of the features is that none of the applied skills apply. It could be a choice, I suppose, but maybe not. Maybe yet another bug. As well, HUD artefacts sometimes just disappear, but luckily your health doesn't matter anyhow, since that one-shot thing is a thing.

I could probably go on, but nah. The thing is, this is an old game that was refreshed and made much, much less playable. Unlike all the folks who can't even get it to run, it does run for me...and that makes it worse, because I got to see (sometimes), hear (sometimes), and feel (way too much) how broken it seems to be.

What I will say is that despite the problems some folks claim are hardware related, I have much more demanding games running very well, so one would think that the team who developed this would have tested it better. But then maybe during testing there were so many graphical glitches they couldn't see what might be broken.

Until the bugs are fixed, there is no way I would recommend this to anyone. 

And...to the studio, this does not bode well for the DLC that is coming, or the Witcher 4. If the former is built on this disastrous foundation, good luck; and if the latter is as buggy as a remaster of a perfectly serviceable old game, the launch is doomed. It won't make any difference how pretty it is, if it is unplayable.

Final verdict 6/10.

The game tries to be some jack of all trades combination of multiple genres, but falls flat due to not perfecting any mechanic.

The only thing Cyberpunk has going for it is the unique and fairly interesting story and the concept of implants. However that's where it falls off and the gameplay quickly becomes stale since the missions are either stealth or loud and both are really underdeveloped.


The stealth is really bland, the NPC's either stand completely still, or move between two points 10 meters apart. Every single mission is the exact same. Walk up to an enemy and press takedown, or distract them with a light and press takedown. Repeat for every enemy. 

The gunplay is also bland and braindead. The enemy AI is useless and either hitscan you from the other side of the map or stand still in front of you and miss absolutely everything.

 The melee combat is complete garbage. You spam R2 without a thought and the enemy hitbox is super clunky, often clipping through cover and teleporting straight on you when dodging or jumping away. The deflect mechanic is also broken, 9/10 times the deflected hit just deals damage anyways. 

The AI is extremely buggy, multiple times a session random cars drive off the road, spawn upside down or crash. You'll also notice that if you drive too close to a sidewalk, the NPC's will almost always glitch and jump BACKWARDS INTO YOUR CAR which gives you wanted level. 60€ btw.

Buy it if you like the style and story, but ONLY  on discount.

comment:
If you have never played this game, now is certainly the time

As far as story, its one of the best for any game I have played, the cutscenes and dialogue are so rich and wonderful compared to what you get out of most AAA games today, not to say that you should go get every line of dialogue, but you will probably wont get bored of it, some of the quests are called Witcher Contracts, where Geralt is hired to kill a monster, it usually starts with Geralt questioning whoever posted the bounty, then investigating the scene of the monsters attack or lair to determine what kind of monster it is, and then the game will give you an update in the codex explaining what oils, potions, bombs, and signs can be useful to help aid you, and then you get a boss battle with the monster, these are some of the best quests in the game for their immersion, each one feels like a proper detective mystery with their twists and turns

As far as tone and writing its really great, the Witcher loves to be in a morally gray mess, where Geralt is forced to choose between two bad options, this makes for really engaging decision making as a player, as you really want to find the right way out, but it keeps it hard to find

As for gameplay, now it is better than its ever been, I play on death march and love it, its punishing at times, but its not masochistic, this is still a game from 2015, its not at all bug free, but its solid, I have played this game thru the main story 3 times and am going for a 4th before Songs of the Past, I only beat Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine last year, when I finally got the game on PC, gameplay does not get stale after this many hours, it didnt even need any gameplay updates for me to want to play it over again for the next DLC either

I love this game and I think you should play it, now that you get the existing DLC for free, to me its a no brainer, tons of extra content, and they arent even gouging you, its a great deal at full price, its an amazing deal on sale, narratively you will be sucked in and the gameplay is good enough to keep you around

comment:
**👎 Not Recommended — Thanks for nothing, Rockstar**

I love GTA V.

I love the GTA series.

I love Rockstar Games.

So naturally, when GTA 6 was announced, I was excited.

And then I remembered one small detail:

**PC players apparently don't exist.**

Apparently my gaming platform is too dangerous for Rockstar to release GTA 6 on at the same time.

Console players get GTA 6.

PC players get…

**GTA V again.**

At this point, GTA V has been released on so many platforms that I'm starting to expect it on my toaster.

And yes, I understand that Rockstar wants to maximize console sales first. Business is business.

But as a PC player who has supported GTA for years, it still feels incredibly frustrating to be treated like the second-class citizen of the GTA community.

We buy the games.

We buy Shark Cards.

We buy the same game approximately 47 times.

And our reward?

**“Coming to PC later.”**

Later™.

No exact date. No proper explanation. Just the classic Rockstar silence.

I know GTA 6 will probably be incredible.

That's exactly why this is so frustrating.

I WANT TO PLAY IT.

I don't want to buy another console just because Rockstar decided PC players can wait.

So yeah:

**Amazing franchise.
Amazing games.
Terrible treatment of PC players.**

I'll probably still buy GTA 6 on PC when it eventually arrives.

Because apparently I'm part of the problem.

**Rockstar: 1
PC players: 0**

See you in Los Santos…

**in 2028, apparently.**

This game made me hate gaming. I think I must be DONE with gaming! Either that or this game just really sucks balls! I've played games like this in the past with these complex systems and figured them out with no problems but the thought of yet ANOTHER one is just fatiguing! 

Maybe my unwillingness to learn the systems is because the story just isnt there for me! Like I said, bad dialogue, hard to understand story! Heres ANOTHER video game thats getting uninstalled! I dont think i'll bother anymore..........Some people may say I have burn out but that couldnt be further from the truth as I am such a casual gamer! I play a game and get really into it and maybe have a few sessions a week for a while and then dont touch a game for weeks!! Im somebody who really WANTS to enjoy gaming like he used to, but I guess with age, your IQ improves and this robs you of enjoying this hobby!

comment:
It was a major disappointment for me. While on paper this game has everything that it needs to be crowned as a masterpiece DLC, and while the first impression upon entering into the DLC provides further merit to that sentiment, very quickly does it fall on its face. 

We have seen this before? This is just an extension of the vanilla late game. Sure a ton of weapons, a ton of bosses and enemies, but at this stage of the game its a bit redundant unless you are ready to reset your character. Its fine to do that but ultimately its just a different path up the same trajectory. 

This vast DLC is... largely empty. It feels like a copy-paste of the altus plateau with slightly darker shades. 

The story, same as in the vanilla, seems very irrelevant. And while this is a staple of From Soft Souls game, in ER it is getting a bit too tiring and not cohesive considering the scale of the game. 

The bosses are the worst offenders. While I'll be the first to admit that I am not a speed/challenge runner, I played all the previous games and enjoyed them vastly. Struggled, sure. But still the bosses were enjoyable. In Shadow of the Erdtree, and ER by and large, the bosses seem without vision or balance. From the peaks of Sekiro and DS3, to bosses here that simply spam attacks, are too large to properly track and read, and generally contain levels of unprecedented bull...  

I wanted to like this DLC and the game. I even gave it a long break, upgraded to fully modern hardware, and watched a bunch of videos about how to properly implement jumping, strafing, and unlocking the camera to better move around bosses and enemies. But putting aside the fact that I am not the best player, the game had failed for me at the simplest level. It had failed to be FUN. Trudging through ER late game and the DLC is a slog. And while the vistas are astonishing... the content and the mechanics fall far, far behind.

Is it a recommendation? Sure, on a technical level it is still a masterpiece that needs to be experienced. The scale of it (while also its downside) is alone a cause for celebration. But a more polished experience with better executed ideas lies in DS3 and Sekiro.

comment:
Elden Ring is the rare open-world game that actually earns its size. The map is huge, but almost every corner has something worth finding - a dungeon, a boss, a weapon, or just a view - and the game never holds your hand toward any of it.

Combat is the usual FromSoftware loop of learning attack patterns and not getting greedy, but the open world and spirit ashes make it more flexible than previous Souls games. You can brute-force a fight, come back later, or summon help. The bosses are the highlight: memorable, hard, and usually fair once you stop panic-rolling.

Build variety is excellent. Strength, magic, faith, and hybrid setups all work, and the weapon types keep things interesting past the first 20 hours. Performance is solid on a decent PC, though the occasional stutter still shows up.

It is long, sometimes opaque, and the late-game difficulty spike is real. If you like figuring things out yourself and don’t mind dying a lot, it’s one of the best games of its kind. About 130 hours in and I’m still finding new stuff.

comment:
Baldur’s Gate 3 gerçekten oyun dünyasında her övgüyü sonuna kadar hak eden bir yapım. Dünyası, karakterleri, atmosferi ve oyuncuya sunduğu özgürlük inanılmaz seviyede. Oyunda yaptığınız en küçük seçimlerin bile ileride karşınıza çıkabilmesi, her oynayışın farklı bir maceraya dönüşmesini sağlıyor.

Özellikle karakterlerin yazımı ve aralarındaki ilişkiler oyunun en güçlü taraflarından biri. Hiçbir karakter sadece görev vermek için dünyaya yerleştirilmiş gibi hissettirmiyor. Her birinin kendi hikâyesi, kişiliği ve amacı var. Fantastik bir dünyada gerçekten kendi hikâyemi yazıyormuşum hissini veren nadir oyunlardan biri.

Savaş sistemi de inanılmaz derecede özgür. Aynı problemi onlarca farklı şekilde çözebilmek, çevreyi kullanmak, büyülerden ve yeteneklerden yaratıcı biçimde yararlanmak oyunu sıradan bir RPG olmaktan çıkarıyor.

Grafikleri kadar atmosferi de etkileyici. Forgotten Realms dünyası hem karanlık hem büyüleyici hissettiriyor ve keşfettiğim her yeni bölge gerçekten merak uyandırıyor.

Kısacası Baldur’s Gate 3 sadece iyi bir RPG değil; oyuncuya özgürlük, seçim ve kendi macerasını yaratma konusunda çıtayı inanılmaz yükseğe koyan bir oyun. Uzun zamandır bir oyunun dünyasına bu kadar fazla emek ve detay işlendiğini görmemiştim. Kesinlikle neslinin en özel RPG’lerinden biri.

I honestly don't know what people see in this game other than the fact that Keanu Reeves comes out in it which is very annoying with his dry bland humor. The mechanics are so bad that if you choose to leave the game for a week and come back, you'll completely forget how to play it because its soooo much mechanics crammed in. Don't get me started with the hacking and braindance. I will try my best not to spoil it. 

Through the game i've found a really annoying bug that happens to overlap dialogue. A character hasn't finished speaking their sentence, and the other character starts on top of their dialogue. Its not game breaking, but it does ruin the immersion. You'll have to rely heavily on subtitles. 

The weapons feel puny. It feels like you have to empty two clips of pure headshots to literally kill an NPC. Night City is a huge open world city that's pretty much...dead. There's nothing to do. Its only alive when your playing missions, but other than that its just vast as an ocean, shallow as a pond. Your very limited to anything really. The slightest crime and you're being chased by random factions that won't stop trying to kill you unless you eliminate them all. 

This game sucks. I rushed my way through the campaign just to say I gave it a try, and its horrible. 1/10.

comment:
So here's an honest review from an RPGer to any D&D fans that expect this to be a masterclass RPG? Nope. As far as a TBS is concerned, this one is fair. It seems to me, lat least in the 1355 hours that I have played, that the game is crafted so that the statistics are about equal between the enemies and your toons at normal level, that is fine. 

What torques my jaw is that-if you choose to play on honor mode-not only do you not have the save handy, but the game just seems to me to give 10-15% statistical bonus to enemies and the same penalty to your toons. Go to honor mode? Probably 20-30% global bonuses and penalties. Not MORE enemies, or higher level enemies that you can see and go "Woah, hey-those guys are level 5" or whatever. No, you see "Lvl 2 Kuo toa" and it will miss once in 5 swings against your level 5 monk with AC 19 and Patient Defense running, while you try and attack their level 2 ass with AC 15 and you will hit about 1 in 5.

Some of you tough kids will say "Y U mad, bro? Play your skill level" and the point is-this ISN'T skill like this: it is foreknowledge of encounters and trying to stack your toon to max statistics and say "♥♥♥♥ the D&D side of it!" I just kind of see it as lazy coding, but these guys started as TBS authors, so they're working their lane, I guess. Just thought some of you looking for an RPG might want to consider something cheaper if a D&D RPG game was your primary interest. Or at least, don't get worked up if your D&D gamer skills don't apply very well here. >.<

comment:
This is my third attempt to get into this game. I'm done.

I want to love it. I've played the previous Baldur's Gate titles, I enjoy the genre, and I'm not looking for hand-holding. What I do want is a narrative that gives me a reason to care about what I'm doing next.

BG3 mistakes "mysterious" for "unclear." There's a brain worm in my head that's supposed to be turning me into a monster — that's a genuinely compelling hook — but the game keeps forgetting to remind me that's the point. I'm following quest markers because the markers exist, not because the story is pulling me forward.

The world is reactive and beautifully constructed. The writing is sharp when it wants to be. But the moment-to-moment narrative momentum is weak. Conversations can collapse into combat without warning. The game withholds information under the guise of tension when it's actually just poor player communication. There's a difference between a mystery that feels earned and one that leaves you genuinely confused about basic decisions.

Three attempts. Uninstalled. The brain worm wins.

comment:
The game is... tedious. 

Let me explain : Exploration does not reward looking IN EVERY CONTAINER or going out of your way to find things. This is especially true in the last act ( city of Baldurs Gate ) where there is HUNDREDS of houses you can break into only to find rags, useless notes or plain equipment that isn't worth much... The loot itself is NOT RANDOMIZED therefore you will always find it in SPECIFIC places which is okay if you have LOADS of equipment... However BG3 has a dozen or so rare / legendary items. Plenty of "Blue / Green" rarity that are very similar to each other making most of them useless. 

I understand that not every game has to have RNG loot but at least put MORE and I mean MORE loot in the game so players are rewarded for exploring / making cool builds. 

Enemy NPC's are blatant CHEATERS. They can see you through WALLS and often then can HIT YOUR THROUGH WALLS TOO! I was inside 2nd story building and the enemy mage shot a fireball which wiped 2 of my characters! THROUGH A FLOOR. Players can't do that. 

There is a potential for subsequent playthroughs BUT I see no point since you can literally RE-SPEC your character at will. Playing as "evil" character doesn't have any appeal to me so after Once doing the campaign I'll be done. 

The game doesn't go on "good" sale despite being released years ago. Can't take my single player character to play with my friends.... instead I have to make a new character that is bound by my friend's save. Now I understand this would break balance and some quests... but I think it would have been possible to have only 1 person the HOST interact with quests / NPC's. 

Either way only recommend on deep sale... if it ever happens.

comment:
This remaster is a disaster. Whoever greenlit its release instead of delaying it seriously needs to be fired. 

I own The Witcher 3 on Steam, PS5, GOG, and Xbox Series X, and I've now tried the remaster across multiple platforms.

On PS5 and Series X, it's essentially unplayable for me. There's constant stuttering while riding Roach and during nearly every combat encounter I've experienced so far. It's a miserable experience, and I won't be playing either console version again until CDPR releases a patch addressing the performance issues. Then there's PC.

Before the remaster, I could comfortably average 90–100 FPS on Ultra settings. After the update, I'm lucky if I can reliably maintain 45–50 FPS. That's an enormous performance hit. Also, the dialogue audio is far too quiet compared to the rest of the mix and I'm constantly having to adjust the volume just to hear characters speaking. 

I've also encountered more bugs in roughly two hours with the remaster than I remember encountering throughout my previous Witcher 3 playthroughs.

This update should have been delayed. There's no good reason it needed to release in this state. I understand that it's a free update, and I appreciate that, but being free doesn't excuse releasing a buggy, poorly optimized remaster with the expectation that the problems can simply be fixed later.

I loved the original Witcher 3, which makes this even more disappointing. But based on my experience across PC, PS5, and Series X, I cannot recommend the remastered version in its current state. Until CDPR addresses the severe performance problems, stuttering, and visual bugs, I'd stay away.

What really confuses me is that even if I turn Path Tracing off, the FPS barely changes. It literally stays around the same. Even switching DLSS to Balanced doesn’t seem to give me any noticeable performance boost. Like… how does that make sense?

The game looks great, don't get me wrong but the poor optimization was enough to make me turn it off.

I absolutely love The Witcher and CDPR, but I have to say, I’m thoroughly disappointed with the performance right now. Hopefully they can sort this out soon because this game deserves better. 

If you really wanna enjoy the masterpiece that is The Witcher 3, play the older version not this heap of a mess.

comment:
🟩 Cyberpunk 2077 & Phantom Liberty – Ultimate Edition  
Now Featuring: "Wait, people said this game was broken?" Edition

>Spent years hearing about the legendary 2020 launch disaster.
>Finally pick up the game post-Update 2.0 alongside Phantom Liberty.
>Brace myself for T-posing NPCs, launching cars, and flatlining save files.
>Instead, get hit with one of the most immersive, visually mind-melting RPGs ever made.
>Keanu Reeves is living rent-free in my head insulting my life choices.
>Idris Elba pulls me into a high-stakes Cold War espionage thriller in Dogtown.
>Look up from my screen: 120 hours have vanished, my V is an untouchable Sandevistan cyber-god dashing through bullets with a katana, and I'm crying over fictional mercenaries at 3 AM.
>Where were the bugs? Did I accidentally buy the right timeline?

10/10 neon depression, 0/10 launch trauma experienced.
CD Projekt Red cooked the greatest redemption arc in modern gaming, and skipping the rough patch was the best decision I ever made.

✅ Night City and Dogtown boast unmatched atmosphere, detail, and verticality
✅ Phantom Liberty’s story and espionage vibe rival the best expansions ever made (Blood and Wine tier)
✅ Update 2.0 combat overhaul turns cyberware builds into pure, addictive power trips
✅ Incredible voice performances from Keanu Reeves and Idris Elba

❌ Existential dread and emotional devastation hitting you in virtually every single ending
❌ Having literally zero relatable "launch day horror stories" to bond over on Reddit
❌ Ruining standard open-world city design for any other game you play afterward

🏙️ Would I recommend the game? 100%. Night City is an absolute masterpiece now.
🦾 Is Phantom Liberty worth getting with it? Non-negotiable. Skipping Dogtown is a straight-up cybercrime.

comment:
elden ring is flawed, very flawed.
a confusing mess of gameplay systems that don't come together as more than the sum of their parts.

the amount of ideas fromsoft had for this game clearly dried up halfway through development, the game's most impactful boss is an obviously repurposed character from sekiro, and the density of gameplay never reaches the level of stormveil castle again. except, maybe, possibly, for leyndell.
pacing of gameplay elements is extremely disjointed, the majority of the game boils down to the world's most obnoxious scavenger hunt.
you run around on your horse for 15 minutes to do a 5 minute long "dungeon" before running around on your horse for 15 more minutes.
collect this weapon, collect this bell bearing, collect this spell, collect a truly ridiculous quantity of materials in an increasingly longer list of stupendous locations to upgrade anything you have.
all in the pursuit of minimizing a difficulty that doesn't exist. the vast majority of the game is trivialized by at least 12 different mechanics. heavy attacks, jump attacks, ashes of war, spells, pots, spirits, twohanding, torrent, great runes, somber weapons, talismans, status effects.
even the most intensive challenge the souls series has to offer, sl0, is practically neutered.
the "longer" areas are a bitter memory of a studio that used to try. the world design of dark souls 3 looks like a masterpiece in comparison. and that game is not stunning either.
at least in that game, you (generally) Can't just sprint to the end of the biggest dungeon in the entire game in about 5 minutes.

don't get me started on the story. from has lost their touch on that front since ds2.

there are brief moments where the game shows it may do something interesting, but that's all they are, moments.
because the fundamental problem is that most of the game is running.
hurray for open world.

comment:
C-bug 1997

since when people have started to give high ratings, highly positive reviews to the broken games? since when and how they became so blind and ignorant?

despite all the false marketing they did back then of this game for being the video game version of the original Cyberpunk rpg boardgame which is released in 1988, i've delayed to play this game for 5 to 6 years, thinking they would eventually fix it...
but what is the end result? the game is still broken and full of bugs.
graphic shaders are burning in the middle of the night city, down on the road. in-game npc characters, enemies and sometimes other half-main characters starts to act weird and even get stuck somewhere.
i've lost the count how many times i had to quick save and reload those saves in order to get the game's command scripts work. because otherwise once the game decides to break itself, it won't simply let you interact with the things or the characters that you need for completing the missions. as if it's a quick save/reload simulator.

𝐍𝐈𝐆𝐇𝐓 𝐂𝐈𝐓𝐘 𝐌𝐀𝐏 - O̶P̶E̶N̶ ̶W̶O̶R̶L̶D̶
this is not even a massive game with extremely large map. the map is very small and the locations which you can have access to is very limited. this alone quickly eliminates any excuses for this game being broken and bug infested even after the 6 years.
apart from the Badlands and some other specific story-related locations, the every part of the city feels all the same as if all the structures and the roads are being copy pasted to everywhere only with slightly applied changes through the indistinguishable editing.
from time to time the city felt and looked like very crowded, yet lacking the liveliness for the immersion.
and you are not completely free to do anything in Night City. you can steal cars, buy cars(not from the physical stores), go to the clothing stores which every one of them has the same outfits without any huge differences and you can go to the ripperdocs for cyberware implementations. and that's just it. because this so called "open world" game doesn't grant you the absolute freedom in its cyberpunk universe.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3736985477
𝐌𝐀𝐈𝐍 𝐒𝐓𝐎𝐑𝐘 - 𝐒𝐈𝐃𝐄 𝐐𝐔𝐄𝐒𝐓𝐒
while few quests were different from one another in a sense of story telling, the essence of the side quests/optional missions is all the same and repetitive.
your objective is very clear and always the same. sneak into some place, eliminate the enemies, secure and collect the things that you need to get for those quests and be done with it. nothing different, just the same tape playing over and over again in monotony.
and since i do not 99% care about any stories in any games i play, the gameplay is the only thing that has the utmost importance for me.
therefore, although i didn't even care about it, the main story was also very much predictable and short.

𝐂𝐇𝐀𝐑𝐀𝐂𝐓𝐄𝐑 𝐂𝐔𝐒𝐓𝐎𝐌𝐈𝐙𝐀𝐓𝐈𝐎𝐍
well... what is there to say about it? no such thing exists in this game, apart from having an option to decide whether you want your character to have genitalia or not.
while there exists some npc characters with a body fully covered with chrome, walking around like androids, you are not able to do any of those full body type of implementations or any other aesthetic-wise stuff you would like to do with your characters body.
and that's all there is to say about the character customization. it simply doesn't exist.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3728569320
𝐑𝐏𝐆 𝐄𝐋𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐍𝐓𝐒
although the CDPR has changed this game's genre tag from rpg to action adventure game back then towards the launch date in an attempt to avoid any fuss it would cause by the people who were actually been waiting for the real rpg game, this one still goes under the rpg tag.
so in case anyone not knows what is the word "RPG" actually means in game genres, let me break it down for you with this game.
RPG simply means "role-playing". and within the role-playing games you usually get to have total freedom of creating your character from scratch, drawing and deciding your character's own unique path where every decision is actually and truly matters.
this game is far and far away from being the real rpg game, same as the 90% of the other games on the store under the same false "RPG" tags (you can curse the popular culture for this falsification).
and that being said, there is no role playing in this game. you can't create your own character from scratch, you can't decide and draw your character's own unique path. everything is pre-determined in this game. and you have no choice but to follow that path without being able to change anything.
you will get different dialogue options with the characters you are interacting and speaking with, but those options hardly affect or change anything.


there are much better game examples than this one in cyberpunk genre, go play them instead.
and start raising a little bit more of your awareness to stop supporting or defending the broken games sold to you by those greedy companies who told lies and did false marketing to deceive their consumers.

comment:
After trying the game for a second time, I still have no idea what is supposed to be fun about it.

I can't stand the graphics, character creation is terrible, dialogue is crap, most characters can be boiled down to "Look at me, I'm so edgy, isn't it cool how edgy I am?", the combat system is a complete slog, animation quality is one of the worst i ever saw, the UI design is the same as original sin... in other words annoying, and the story is just not that interesting

it's cool that people like this game I guess, but I finished hundreds of games and played thousands. If you want a cool rpg that lasts 50+ hours you're better off looking at pathfinder kingmaker / wrath of the righteous, xenoblade chronicles, digimon story cyber sleuth / time stranger, hundred line, crosscode, final fantasy (any of them), sea of stars, or disco elysium.

EDIT:
because some people have reading comprehension of a goldfish and are too butthurt when someone criticises their "perfect" game, let me expand on this review a lot more I guess.

The way to describe Baldur's Gate 3 would be that the game is very, very wide, but also incredibly shallow. And I honestly think if Larian had about half the budget and actually thought about what to do with the game, it could have been a lot better.

Now, let me expand on why "I can't stand the graphics."
Overall I despise most games that are trying to do photorealistic graphics, in 99% of cases it looks disgusting to me. Good graphics don't need to be anime or cartoony or some kind of vivid spectacle. But if you want photorealistic graphics I would heavily consider stylizing them around something, or make the graphics just insanely good. 
Like Alan wake 2 is photorealistic, but it puts insanely high focus on environments and it's very noisy in its presentation, plus it's horror and very high fidelity, so it looks good. Which is probably another point, remedy uses real actors and the characters looks not just photorealistic but real. Which most games fail to do and the fake photorealism is inherently wrong. 
That's a stance on graphic design I will die on. Almost every AAA game puts emphasis on graphics and pretty much all of them fail miserably. 

Animation in baldurs gate 3 is something you can't defend, it's utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Characters simply stand in place and talk, in a very rigid pose with almost no emotion. And then when they need to move they suddenly get into an animation that is incredibly choppy and then they go back to standing and talking. There is absolutely no fluidity or movement to it, no emotion behind character actions. 
Even the scene where if you play a bard you get to do a whole song, while the song itself is pretty nice and the narrative around it is actually kinda cool, watching your character do that song is taking you out of it. Which again, photorealistic graphics with very rigid 3d models is the fault at bad animation. 

Which also ties to character creation, where you can't complain much about DND choices, it's copying a system and the system itself is by my standard terrible. But the visual creation is bad... Which is still connected to graphics, but it's insanely difficult to make a character that looks pretty and there are no sliders or anything, there's like 8 preset faces and most of them are ugly as ♥♥♥♥. 
Hair selection is probably the only good thing there. And it's cool you can look at your ♥♥♥♥ but overall the game doesn't really do much with nudity anyway. If you give me an option to have a dangling penis between my legs then have a decency of letting me use it as well xD 
But another thing, some people will see a lot of races and subraces. They are all humans. Human with pointy ears. Short human with a beard. Even gith are just humans with ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up faces. The only non humanoid option is dragonborn and the only reason it is an option is because larian already have lizard models from original sin. 
The beauty of playing a fantasy game is playing nonhuman fantasy races. The very least we could have gotten was tabaxi. But their photorealistic graphics don't allow for individuality. 

Everyone is edgy wasn't exactly the criticism, I didn't really specify it, so that's on me. But the criticism would be "overly edgy". You can have good edgy characters. But bg3 companions are incredibly shallow and one noted. 
I keep hearing they get a lot better and deeper once you get far enough and explore the dialogue options but that's not something I'm willing to discover. Wasting 30+ hours on finding out that the character is not an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is too much time. 
You can write mysterious and intriguing characters without making them obnoxious. 

Combat is something I didn't enjoy in original sin as well, and it's practically the same here. It is deceptively complex. You can in theory spend a lot of time optimizing and strategizing but in the end it's all just dice rng that can heavily make or break the entire combat. On higher difficulty it could be different and all, but it's not a type of game to play for difficult combat, the story and characters are the main drawing point, so playing on normal or even lower is fair. 
And there the combat just slogs through because you're given a lot of options for very little value, often to your own detriment actually when just clicking an enemy for normal attack is gonna do a lot more than anything else. And it just slogs in round after round. 
You might say that pathfinder is even worse but that's not true because pathfinder has that granular strategy that can heavily change outcomes of combats. Plus pathfinder does have real time with pause so you can fast forward through trash fights while focusing more tactically in turned based on boss fights. It's stupidly difficult and often also boiled down to ♥♥♥♥♥♥ dice rng. But it is a lot more complex and rewarding because of it. 
Slog doesn't mean it takes long, just that the amount of time taken is not satisfying. And BG3 combat is not satisfying in any way.

comment:
This is a very difficult review for me and I cannot show all my motivations in this section, after all if you are reading this you want a quick opinion before you buy the game.

First of all, I’m sure that most of this reviews here are from genuinely honest people that enjoyed this game, and I can see why. The mechanics are impressive, the implementation of powers, spells, skills it’s a breath of innovation; for the most part the game feels alive with interaction of NPC, great voice acting, choices and consequences. 
If this game was called something like “Legends of Forgotten Realms” or “Heroes of the Sword Coast” and wasn’t connected in any way from the previous Baldur’s Gate saga I would love this game 100%.
But sadly it is not.

The fact is, in my opinion, Baldur’s Gate 2 Throne of Bhaal was the perfect ending for the saga, maybe a little rushed  (the developers they were hurrying due to the upcoming shutting down of the company).
A book also from those years established the canon ending, clearly stating the fate of most of the notable characters, even the Bhaal Spawn.
I played dozens of time BG and BG2 plus the expansions, I shared those moments with the community of the time and we appreciate the character’s arch and stories of each one. 

 Then Wizard of the Coast released the modules Descent to Avernus and Murder in Baldur’s Gate, compromising the endings from the awesome series by reintroducing PNG that were supposed to be elsewhere or not existing. 
And probably Larian’s writers did even worst, [spoiler]by no respecting the few good canonic elements and reconnecting the main plot to the previous BG chapters.[/spoiler] 
All because they want to grab more income by squeezing a well loved brand that most people out there do not remember so well anymore. 
Larian had the resource  to write an all new story, a new brand for a spectacular title. Instead they lacked courage by playing safe.
Also I want to mention the impressive presence of bugs related to sub quest, graphical errors that breaks the immersion  especially in the last chapter of the game. Considering the game was in early access for a very long time (full price around 60 bucks) and the use of AI during the last period of develop this is a very reprehensible conduct. 
I do not reported the bugs and errors I encountered during my experience.

My only hope is in the newer generation of player. Who may enjoy good stories, who may discover the first games and who wants to appreciate the old adventures and perfect ending… do not stop on the surface and find out how the game industry was different back then. 

I know we are not so many anymore and maybe this message is not important; but if YOU are like me, a real fan of BG, do not buy this game. It’s an insult to all the original BG’s writers and the gamers who loved the series.

comment:
It's the Witcher 3... of course it's great but the remaster is a different story all together. I've never been one to complain about game performance because I have always had old hardware and understood that it's just what I get for not paying for the latest tech. 

Since then however, I have upgraded to a 9070 XT and can run demanding titles with 100fps on 34inch ultrawide 3440x1440 without any frame gen. This includes titles like GOW Ragnarock (stable above 300fps) and Ghost of Tsushima which are graphically stunning. 

When I heard about the remaster, I was excited to play one of the best games of all time on my new hardware but the performance means that I simply can't enjoy it at all. I can't get anything above a complete slideshow 20fps with pathtracing on. Without it, the best I can get is an unstable 55fps and that's with frame generation on..... 

I understand that the graphical improvements would make the game perform worse but this game, despite improvements, still looks worse (on account of still being over 10 years old) than almost all other games I can run at 100+ fps. 

For anyone considering buying the Witcher 3 now and playing it on PC, unless you have a literal data center at your disposal than wait a while because the performance might hurt your experience of what is for many the single best title ever made. 

Will definetely change to positive if and when these problems are resolved.

CD Projekt Red lied to customers, admitted they did so, apologized for it, then charged for the content they cut with the Phantom Liberty DLC. How are people defending the Phantom Liberty DLC? The Johnny Silverhand storyline is decent, don't get me wrong, but you are essentially watching his story. You are a part of his conundrum and journey from being a rebellious rockstar to a titan taking down Arasaka and Militech. I even tested multiple storylines by saving and retrying dialogue to see what the different outcomes would be, but it's meaningless. It's about as bad as Fallout 4. People are high on copium wishing this game was what they were hoping for before release in 2018. They got duped and feel stupid for it, so they've convinced themselves it's good when it's not. comment:
Beware, this game is nothing like Baldur's Gate, TOSC, Shadows of Amn or Throne of Bhaal.
So far it seems like nothing is remotely similar except that the city of Baldur's gate is supposed to feature in it at some point. I'm not trying to say this is a bad game, it is AFAIK keeping quite true to D&D and appears as though it's a very high quality crpg of D&D fifth edition( ...? I think it's the fifth edition, it did say but I wasn't really paying attention). 
My problem is that it isn't remotely true to Baldur's Gate games in a gameplay sense. It is turn based, combat is very slow, you have to wait for everyone to take their turns. I don't like this.
You have no party formations, although that doesn't actually matter anyway. 
You constantly have to roll things and watch a picture of a dice to see if you can: open a chest; persuade a character; scratch your balls etc. etc....

Oh and btw, for some reason Larian have felt the need to include removable underwear and fully rendered genitals. IDK wtf for exactly, maybe at some point in the game you get to roll your luck with someone and have a full cut scene D&D porno, but I digress. Some people really like this sort of thing and it's not for me to disparage them (nor is it my intention, I just find it curious that they spent the time to render all those ♥♥♥♥♥).

I'm not really that far into the game ATM, the story I've come across is well done and well thought out and the 3d world is very impressively detailed, it is somewhat challenged in terms of scale compared to previous games in the series as far as I can see though. Not that some of the previous games didn't squash a bit too much in here and there, but I'm still in the first region you get to and already the scales of time and distance seem horrendously warped. 
A character I picked up (easily missed btw) has just said how much they trust me after we've been travelling together for a few days. This occurred the first time I went to camp for a full rest. Which is also weird, that I have a camp set up for a bunch of people to stay at because for some reason nobody can travel in a group larger than four and also, I JUST GOT HERE, when did I go and set up this camp, when did I find this remarkable hideaway, seemingly safe from/for all....?

Honestly I believe it would have been better if they'd kept expanding on Siege of Dragonspears' method: Keep making what people have loved for twenty odd years.

comment:
Elden Ring is genuinely one of the best games I've ever played.

The exploration is incredible. You can pick a direction, wander off, and somehow end up finding an entire castle, underground city, or boss that you had absolutely no idea existed. The combat is satisfying, the build variety is ridiculous, and the feeling of finally beating a boss that's been kicking your ass for an hour is something very few games can replicate.

It's not perfect. Some bosses can be frustrating as hell, the PC performance has had its issues, and occasionally the game seems determined to remind you that you are, in fact, terrible at it.

But overall? Elden Ring is an incredible game and absolutely deserves the praise it gets.

Unfortunately, the Tarnished Pack is where FromSoftware and Bandai Namco completely lost me.

$5 for two starting classes, a handful of armor and weapons, some NPC invasions, and three cosmetic skins for Torrent is already pushing it. But the fact that some of the equipment can be obtained in-game anyway makes charging for this feel even more ridiculous.

And then they bundle this content with the new Switch 2 version while turning around and telling the people who already bought and supported the game on other platforms to pay extra for it.

Seriously?

This isn't a real expansion. This isn't Shadow of the Erdtree. Shadow of the Erdtree gave us an entire new world to explore, bosses, weapons, enemies, and dozens of hours of content. That was DLC worth paying for.

The Tarnished Pack feels like they looked at a small amount of bonus content that could have been a free update and decided, "Nah, let's charge them for it."

And before someone says, "It's only $5," I genuinely do not care. The price does not magically make bad DLC practices okay. If anything, it's the principle of it. Elden Ring has sold millions of copies. People have supported this game for years, bought Shadow of the Erdtree, and helped make it one of the biggest games of the last decade.

So rewarding those players by making them pay extra for a couple of starting classes and horse cosmetics while giving the content to new Switch 2 buyers as part of their edition is just insulting.

I still love Elden Ring. The actual game is phenomenal.

But I'm not going to pretend the Tarnished Pack isn't a blatant attempt to squeeze more money out of an already massively successful game.

comment:
This is perhaps the hardest review I have ever had to write, because I literally have to recommend against playing what I think is a great game, but I cannot, because it is marred by a thick buggy web that prevents my enjoyment of it.

So first off, the game does have some great characters, excellent musical score, an interesting world / plot, and an overwhelming amount of choices you can make so that no 2 playthroughs are alike. The writing can be a bit weak / contrived at times, but this is a D&D high fantasy game, it comes with the territory.

The game is split into 3 acts, and Act 1 is absolutely brilliant. It's a slow burn that really gives you time to warm up to the gameplay and learn how the combat works, but it doesn't hold you hand so much that it hampers that feeling of natural exploration and discovery. My how I loved act I.

Then comes Act II.... and well, the game starts to break down. Plots resolve incorrectly, progression doesn't work randomly for some quests, enemy AI kept breaking. The nonsense just kept piling up, but I was having a good enough time I could ignore most of it.

Then Act III, which is larger than Act 1 and 2 combined. It's a disaster, SO MANY quest bugs. SO MANY issues with the enemy AI. Things that worked ok in Act 1 and 2 are just broken here. My characters would glitch through doors randomly, when I issued commands in combat, the character would start to take the action, nothing would happen, then I lose my action. Jumping is just all out broken, my characters would freeze in mid air then would make the death falling noise and I would take damage. Enemies would freeze in combat and do nothing for a full 10+ seconds, EVERY. SINGLE, ROUND, making it a nightmare of a slog to get through a single combat. I would often focus down enemies simply because their AI was bugging out and I just couldn't standing watching them sit their and drool while doing nothing again.

I can put up with A LOT for a good game, but no matter how good BG3 is otherwise, it's just to much to bear. The game seems to be getting worse with each patch, which is mind boggling. This game needs to be rebuilt from the ground up in a working engine, because this is just not a good experience as is. I honestly don't think most of the people reviewing this game well made it through Act 3, because there is no way you can ignore this many issues.

Maybe the game works better on consoles, that could be worth looking into as it's a real shame to miss out on such a good narrative experience, especially since this is perhaps the most epic D&D based game ever released. I really wish the studio that made it had let it cook longer, but oh well, not much we can do now.

comment:
I highly recommend playing and actually finishing Elden Ring and its DLC, because sticking with it to the very end is where it truly shines. The game refuses to hold your hand or plaster markers all over your map, forcing you to genuinely explore, get lost, and discover hidden items and strange NPCs on your own. While I thought the game was fine after my first playthrough, going through it again and really paying attention to the story and lore made me realize just how wonderful and deep the worldbuilding actually is to the point where I would spend time watching lengthy YouTube videos about the lore of the game. 

The official co-op and summoning mechanics could definitely be better and feel a bit restrictive, the modding scene on PC easily fixes that by running mods like Seamless Co-op and plenty others to transform the multiplayer gameplay into a more enjoyable and hassle-free experience with friends.

Overall, 9/10 for me!

comment:
Will update this review once problems are solved. In its current remastered state, I can't really recommend it FOR PLAY ON THE STEAM DECK, which is my main modality of play. 

On PC, with decent specs, it runs perfectly fine no issues with the remastered. If anything, the remastered edition looks a lot better, textures are less washed out, contrast is better, and the systems overhaul is pretty nice. However, playing it on the steam deck LCD is a different story. 

Pre-update I was able to play either locked 40fps native stable, or 30fps upscaled to 60fps with LSFG-VK 2.0 and have minimal input lag and smooth frametimes. Played like a dream to where I was (middle of Velen questlines). Post-update with the remastered, this is no longer possible. Running things at absolute lowest settings possible (lower than steam deck preset) WITHOUT LSFG feels like there's about 250ms of input lag and frametimes spike from 20-80ms, very unstable. With LSFG-VK 2.0 at 2x, optimized settings, input lag feels about 150-200ms but artifacts and tearing are a huge problem, no real improvements to frametimes either. Deck runs at about a constant 85-90C, so there's small room for graphical improvements, but none that would matter for stability or performance. This is what I consider unplayable. It's not LSFG producing the issues, the game literally cannot maintain stable 30fps in medium intensity areas, even at 1280x800 resolution, much less Novigrad. Yes, you can revert the game to pre-update status, but then why do the remastered update in the first place?

I don't doubt that they'll make performance updates over time, but in its current state, I cannot recommend it for the modality I play the game on. As with everything, YMMV, though.

comment:
1/10 — The Hackers Have Better Anti-Cheat Than the Developers
This game somehow managed to achieve an incredibly impressive feat – the actual enemy team isn’t the biggest problem here. The real monster is the anti-cheat.
Every single match is a competition of cheaters to see who can cheat more – wallhacks, aimbots, impossible tracking, headshots through walls – you name it, and at this point, I’m not even surprised. I’m not asking “how can they do this?” – I’m begging “how long are they going to let this happen?”
The very fact that the game’s “developers” allow this to happen is part of the issue, though
It’s wild how fast they could implement new skins, bundles, battle passes, events and other assorted cash grabs, but apparently, detecting a player who can spin around 5 times per second and wipe out an entire team while invisible through walls is too hard for their tiny team of developers to handle.
I can spend hours upon hours upon hours upon hours dedicated to improving my aim, learning the map, discovering new strategies and playing the game as it is supposed to be played – only for someone with a fresh account and a cheat to come into my lobby and turn it into a glorified target practice. I will report them, receive my prize of an empty “report received” message and pray that the next match won’t be another round of Hackerman Simulator 2026.
But what’s worse is that cheating in this game – and the lack of anti-cheat measures – destroy the game from the inside. The very premise of a competitive FPS is ruined when it’s possible to simply install a better cheat. Why would players invest time and money into the game if they can simply “download miracle cheat 3.0” and become the best player in the world?
The developers could have solved this problem in the past, but instead, they give us empty speeches about “community reports” and “dedicated servers”, giving us the same tired answers over and over again:
Hackers appear → players complain → devs promise action → nothing meaningful changes → hackers come back.
 It’s not funny anymore. The competitive FPS genre revolves around trust – and this single fact has been understood by cheat creators from day one. This development team, however, apparently does not have a brain, and that is a serious problem. The enemy team isn’t even the problem.At this point, the hackers aren’t cheating – they’re testing the quality of the anti-cheat and the dedication of the developers. Good gunplay, potentially fun gameplay, ruined by the feeling that I am playing the game against not opponents, but an army of script Kiddies who enjoy cheating. Will not be purchasing any time or items from this dev team until they show some dedication to fixing the game.

what is left to say about this game that hast been said already, the absolute mastery of the craft that fromsoft shows time and time again is flooring, they are one of the few developers that you can trust to always deliver something special and ER is the best example of this.

I remember my first playthrough all those years ago now, the map just kept zooming out and out and the world felt never ending. Its to the point where last week while i was on my 20 something run of the game or more i STILL discovered a path down to an area id never seen before. I remember the first time i found all the hidden cities, the first time i entered caelid by accident, the first time that i discovered that a random cave in a random beach leads down to an interconnected network of underground tunnels full of bugs, viscera and magic that leads you to one of the endings of the game. The sheer amount of love that's put into carefully crafting this world is nothing short of incredible and while there is a couple of caveats to that the game overall is a masterpiece. I can only hope that the next big thing that fromsoft works on doesn't get scope creeped by this and they're able to deliver something just as special even if its different. 

As a side note I do fear a little bit for the future of fromsoft, with them getting bought out by sony majorly i can already see some ill omens for the company, first was nightreign that i haven't played yet but i think making a whole game as a multiplayer asset flip is far from what miyazaki would've done if he still had the final say, same thing with the duskbloods. I still however believe that whatever fromsoft intends to do for their next mainline game will be fantastic, as it normally is.

comment:
Baldur's Gate 3, while decent, is extremely overhyped and underwhelming.
Having played both Baldur's Gate 1 and 2 to death, and loving every moment of it, I was severely disappointed in how they handled its nominal successor.

Where BG1 and BG2 gave a long, intricate, story-rich adventures that felt like they spanned a full country's worth of areas, BG3 offers three and a half areas (the Underdark area of part 1) with a small bit of story, and a few sidequests here and there. 

It also comes with its fair share of annoyances, such as:
-Not being able to pause, ever, citing "you don't need to!" as their reason (it's usually true, but absolutely not 100% so).
-When engaged in conversation with a person or an object, it's *always* the character initiating the conversation (on purpose or by accident) that does the skill check, regardless of how (un)realistic it would be for them to do so (here they could have learned a ton from the creators of the Pathfinder games)
-Time only being counted through long rests makes the game less immersive
-Inventory handling is a mess
-Being able to teleport items to your camp is unimmersive
-Being able to teleport to and from your camp at will (outside combat) is unimmersive
-Movement in combat is buggier than it should be
-Several instances of mechanics or effects are mentioned and never explained, leaving it as an exercise to the reader to attempt to work out what they do (i.e. google it, and hope to avoid spoilers in the process - they show up in the dumbest places)
-Only four party members at a time leaves less room for party dynamics and "on-the-fly" story
-Almost all party members are highly good-aligned, leaving you with almost no choices if you want an evil-aligned campaign with members that have a story

In sum:
BG3 is far smaller, shorter and less engaging than the originals, and only does one thing better than them: Graphics and voice acting, which seems to be where they put 70% of their time and effort, despite this being a *roleplaying game*. If you like RPGs, play all the other good ones before you bother with this one (on sale).
